svg.title: Protein processing: location and order
svg.desc: Phosphorylation can turn activity up or down. Proinsulin folds with disulfide bonds before C-peptide removal. Secretory glycosylation occurs in ER and Golgi; nuclear cytoplasmic O-GlcNAc cycles locally.
svg.text: Protein processing: location and order matter
1 A phosphate is a switch—not always “on”
Kinase adds phosphate • phosphatase hydrolyzes it off
Outcome: activity ↑ or ↓, depending on protein and site
2 Insulin: fold first, then remove C-peptide
Signal peptide removed → proinsulin in the ER
Proinsulin folds and forms three disulfide bonds
Mature insulin retains the disulfide-bonded A + B chains
N-linked glycans: initial transfer in ER → ER/Golgi processing
Nuclear/cytoplasmic O-GlcNAc: OGT adds; OGA removes
These processes do not share one universal location or switch.
